channel.title: Bay Area Sports Blog
channel.description: Every Bay Area team, argued about properly. The 49ers, Warriors, Giants, A's and Sharks, written by a fan, not a network.

item.title: Brock Purdy Is 147 Passes From Being the Most Efficient Quarterback in NFL History. Nobody Wants to Say It Out Loud.
item.description: Brock Purdy's career passer rating is 104.0. The all-time record is Aaron Rodgers at 102.2. Purdy has 1,353 career attempts and the record requires 1,500 — about five games into the 2026 season, he qualifies, and the record is his.

item.title: They Finally Gave Brock Purdy a Fight. He Won It Going Away.
item.description: The most competitive practice of 49ers camp yet — offense and defense trading haymakers on 87 Day — and Brock Purdy went 12-of-17 on 32 team snaps and ran the whole thing. Raheem Morris is calling him the Layer King.

item.title: The Giants Got Marcelo Mayer for a Reliever Who Walks Everybody. Explain That One, Boston.
item.description: The Red Sox traded Marcelo Mayer — the fourth overall pick in 2021 and recently one of the best prospects in baseball — to the Giants for Erik Miller, a 28-year-old lefty reliever who has walked nearly 16 percent of the hitters he has faced. On paper this is a robbery.

item.title: The 49ers Signed KhaDarel Hodge, and That Tells You Everything About This Receiver Room
item.description: The 49ers added 31-year-old veteran wide receiver KhaDarel Hodge, a Pro Bowl special teamer with Raheem Morris ties, because the receiver room is falling apart in August. Again.

item.title: Brock Purdy Is Carving Up Training Camp. Twenty Guys Watched Him Do It From the Sideline.
item.description: Brock Purdy went 13-of-14 in team drills and accounted for three straight touchdowns in a red zone period. Meanwhile the 49ers had twenty players unavailable on August 5, 2026 — Kittle, Bosa, Greenlaw, Kirk, Evans, Juszczyk and a growing list.

item.title: Four Signings in a Week: Okoronkwo, Irwin, Deguara, Hodge, and a Roster Held Together With Tape
item.description: The 49ers signed edge rusher Ogbo Okoronkwo, wide receivers Trenton Irwin and KhaDarel Hodge, and tight end Josiah Deguara inside a week. Every one of them makes sense. That is exactly what worries me.

item.title: Reds 3, A's 2: Jacob Lopez Struck Out Nine on 87 Pitches, Kotsay Took Him Out Anyway, and the Streak Hit Seven
item.description: Jacob Lopez struck out nine over five innings on 87 pitches and Mark Kotsay went to the bullpen anyway. Two batters later the lead was gone. The Athletics lost 3-2 in Cincinnati on August 5, 2026 for their seventh straight defeat, falling to 45-69.

item.title: Rangers 6, Giants 0: Eleven Men Left On Base, Zero for Eight With Runners in Scoring Position, and Nineteen Games Under .500
item.description: The Giants got shut out 6-0 in Arlington on August 5, 2026, left 11 men on base, went 0-for-8 with runners in scoring position, and fell to 48-67 — nineteen games under .500 for the first time all season.

item.title: Purdy Is Ripping It in Camp, and That Throw to Demarcus Robinson Was a Dime
item.description: Brock Purdy looks sharp as anything at 49ers camp, and he dropped an absolute dime to Demarcus Robinson in the back of the end zone over two defenders. Anticipation, touch, no hesitation. Just stay healthy, BCB.

item.title: The 49ers Love Raheem Morris, and It Is Because He Lets Them Play Football
item.description: Raheem Morris took over the 49ers defense and the first thing everybody noticed was the joy. Five-down looks, new coverages, Warner and Greenlaw back together, and a coordinator who tells guys to go play instead of drowning them in a call sheet. Finally.

item.title: Reds 5, A's 4: They Led in the Eighth and Lost on Wild Pitches. Plural. Wild Pitches.
item.description: The Sacramento A's took a 4-3 lead into the eighth in Cincinnati and gave the game away on two wild pitches — the tying run and the winning run both scored without the ball being put in play. J.T. Ginn's solid return wasted. A's fall to 45-68.

item.title: Heliot Ramos Is a Yankee: The Rest of the Selloff We Have Not Talked About
item.description: Buster Posey traded Heliot Ramos to the Yankees, Erik Miller to the Red Sox for Marcelo Mayer, and Tyler Mahle to the Braves. Five trades, eight new names, and the homegrown kid we developed is hitting in the Bronx now.

item.title: Rangers 5, Giants 4: Vitello Sat Bryce Eldridge, Eldridge Tied the Game Off the Bench Anyway, and the Ninth Inning Lost It Anyway
item.description: Tony Vitello kept Bryce Eldridge out of the starting lineup, Eldridge came off the bench and tied it with a two-run single in the ninth, and the Giants still lost 5-4 in Arlington on a walk-off double. San Francisco falls to 48-66.

item.title: It Is August and the 49ers Are Already Hurt. Again.
item.description: Pearsall is having season-ending knee surgery, Kittle and Mykel Williams are on PUP, and the injury report grows by the day at 49ers camp. Nobody has hit anybody yet and we are already counting bodies. This is not bad luck anymore.

item.title: Arraez Is Gone: The Best Hitter We Had Is a Phillie Now
item.description: The Giants traded Luis Arraez and Caleb Kilian to the Phillies for two right-handed pitching prospects. The National League batting leader, the one guy in the lineup who never gave away an at-bat, is gone. This is what selling looks like when you are the one being sold from.

item.title: Robbie Ray to the Padres: Of Course It Is the Padres. Of Course It Is.
item.description: Robbie Ray is reportedly headed to San Diego at the deadline. Nothing is official yet. But the Giants are about to hand a Cy Young winner to the team that just swept them, and that tells you everything about where this season ended up.

item.title: Tigers 11, A's 0: Swept, Shut Out, and Outscored 32-7 in Three Days
item.description: Gage Jump walked six and did not finish the fourth, Detroit poured on four more in the eighth, and a position player finished the game. The A's are 45-67, losers of five straight, and outscored 32-7 in the series.

item.title: Padres 5, Giants 4: Swept in San Diego, Four Walks in the Second, and a Deadline That Cannot Come Fast Enough
item.description: Landen Roupp walked four and gave up five, the Giants chipped back three times and never got even, and San Francisco got swept out of Petco Park. They are 47-65 with the deadline hours away.

item.title: Ricky Pearsall Is Out for the Year, and This Kid Just Cannot Catch a Break
item.description: Ricky Pearsall is headed for season-ending PCL surgery and will miss all of 2026. A gut punch for a 49ers receiver who has never once gotten a clean, healthy run at his career.

item.title: Padres 6, Giants 5: Osleivis Basabe Tied It Off a 103-MPH Fastball, and the Ninth Inning Threw It Away
item.description: A guy playing his third game of the season did everything, the Giants clawed back from 5-3 in the eighth, and then Jake Cronenworth walked it off in the ninth. Ninth loss column entry in San Diego, and the Giants drop to 47-64.

item.title: Tony Vitello Has No Idea What He Is Doing With This Lineup, and Bryce Eldridge Batting Leadoff Is the Proof
item.description: Sixty different batting orders in seventy-seven games. Eight different leadoff hitters. And now the 21-year-old middle-of-the-order bat is hitting first. Vitello was the worst hire this franchise has made in a decade and the lineup card proves it every single day.

item.title: Monday's Deadline Is the Only Interesting Thing Left About This Season, and Buster Posey Cannot Blink Again
item.description: Forty-seven and sixty-four. Ten games out. Heliot Ramos on the block, Jung Hoo Lee reportedly staying, Arraez and Ray on expiring deals, and a bullpen that has cost this team a dozen games. If Posey does not tear it down Monday, he never will.

item.title: Deebo Samuel Is Coming Home: 49ers Bring Him Back on a One-Year, $7 Million Deal
item.description: Deebo Samuel is returning to San Francisco on a one-year, $7 million deal. A low-risk, high-reward reunion that adds another physical, versatile weapon to an already loaded 49ers offense.

item.title: De'Zhaun Stribling Keeps Balling Out in Camp, and a Starting Job Is Starting to Look Inevitable
item.description: The 49ers' rookie wide receiver De'Zhaun Stribling isn't just flashing anymore, he's stacking good days on top of good days at training camp. At this rate, a Week 1 starting job is starting to look like the floor, not the ceiling.

item.title: Dre Greenlaw Hit Too Hard on Day One of Pads, and Christian McCaffrey Still Calls Him His Favorite Player
item.description: The first padded practice of 49ers training camp turned physical fast once Dre Greenlaw started delivering hits, and Christian McCaffrey didn't hide that he wasn't thrilled about it. He's also said Greenlaw is his favorite player in the league. Both things are true, and that's exactly why this team is different.

item.title: Kyle Shanahan Update: He's Turning the Corner, and Camp Is Feeling It
item.description: Pads are on at 49ers training camp, and Kyle Shanahan is edging closer to fully running the show again after his July 14 car accident. An update on where his recovery stands as camp ramps up.

item.title: Padres 7, Giants 0: Two Hits. Two. That Is the Whole Night.
item.description: Carson Whisenhunt could not get out of the fourth, San Diego walked all over a lineup that managed two hits in nine innings, and the good feeling from Thursday lasted exactly twenty-four hours. Giants fall to 47-63.

item.title: The A's Free Fall Never Actually Stopped: 45-63, Fourth Place, and a Trade Deadline That Can't Come Soon Enough
item.description: Nine straight losses into the All-Star break was supposed to be the bottom. Instead the Athletics have gone 4-8 since, they are 18 games under .500 in fourth place, and Monday's trade deadline is arriving right on schedule for a team with nothing left to sell but time.

item.title: The Giants Are Playing Their Best Baseball of the Season, and the Brewers Series Just Proved It
item.description: Forget the record for a second. Over the last five games the Giants beat the best team in baseball twice, walked one off in extra innings, and hung sixteen runs on a 67-win club. This is the best they have looked all year.

item.title: Kyle Shanahan's Car Accident Was Scarier Than We Knew, and Niner Nation Just Needs Him Healthy
item.description: Kyle Shanahan was banged up far worse than anyone realized in his July 14 car accident — a severe concussion, a broken nose, three broken ribs, a broken hand, and over 40 stitches. He'll be limited early in training camp while Chris Foerster picks up some of the load, and all that matters right now is that he heals up.

item.title: Purdy and Rookie De'Zhaun Stribling Are Already Cooking, and This Niners Roster Is Loaded
item.description: Brock Purdy and rookie wideout De'Zhaun Stribling are building real chemistry, and with Mike Evans and George Kittle in the fold, Christian McCaffrey and Trent Williams anchoring the offense, and Fred Warner, Nick Bosa, and Dre Greenlaw all back healthy, the 49ers look as dangerous as they've been in years.

item.title: Red Sox 4, Athletics 2 (10): Jacob Lopez Deals, the Offense Sleeps, Extras Bite Again
item.description: Jacob Lopez strikes out eight, Jonah Heim and Lawrence Butler both homer, and the A's still lose in ten when Andruw Monasterio takes Jose Suarez deep. A's fall to 45-63.

item.title: Giants 16, Brewers 3: The Offense Finally Erupted, and It Was Glorious
item.description: Seventeen hits. A seven-run sixth. Daniel Susac's first two career home runs. The Giants hung 16 on the best team in baseball and took the series from the Brewers.

item.title: How Steve Kerr Actually Handled Jonathan Kuminga
item.description: It was never as clean as 'buried him' or 'stood by him.' Kerr's handling of Jonathan Kuminga was a season-long negotiation between a coach who needed shooting and spacing right now, and a 22-year-old who needed the ball to become what the front office paid him to become.

item.title: Athletics 4, Red Sox 3: Brian Serven's Homer Holds Up, Tommy White Goes 4-for-4
item.description: Gage Jump worked six scoreless, Brian Serven's two-run homer in the seventh broke a scoreless game open, and Tommy White went 4-for-4, and it was all just enough as Hogan Harris survived a two-run ninth to close out a 4-3 Athletics win over the Red Sox in Sacramento.

item.title: Brewers 8, Giants 2: Landen Roupp Never Found It, Bryce Eldridge's Homer Was the Only Answer
item.description: Landen Roupp lasted just 3.2 innings and allowed four runs as Milwaukee piled up 13 hits, and Bryce Eldridge's eighth-inning two-run homer was the only real answer the Giants had in an 8-2 loss to the Brewers at Oracle Park.

item.title: Red Sox 4, Athletics 2: Ceddanne Rafaela's First Career Slam Beats a Costly No-Hit Bid
item.description: Jack Perkins held Boston to one hit for five-plus innings before Ceddanne Rafaela's first career grand slam broke it open in the sixth, and Tyler Soderstrom and Jonah Heim's solo homers were not enough as the Athletics fell 4-2 to the Red Sox in Sacramento.

item.title: Giants 3, Brewers 0: Tyler Mahle and Grant McCray Shut the Best Team in Baseball Down
item.description: Tyler Mahle spun six shutout innings, Grant McCray's two-run homer in the fourth did all the damage the Giants needed, and Erik Miller closed it out as San Francisco blanked the 66-win Brewers 3-0 at Oracle Park. Giants improve to 45-61.

item.title: The Warriors' Front Office Keeps Failing Steph Curry, and "He Could Leave" Doesn't Sound Crazy Anymore
item.description: Wasted draft capital, half-measure trades, and a supporting cast that keeps aging out from under him. The front office has strained Steph Curry's patience for years, and for the first time, imagining him somewhere else doesn't feel absurd.

item.title: Twins 11, Athletics 8: Down 7-0 Before Springs Left Hurt, and the Hole Was Just Too Deep
item.description: Jeffrey Springs lasted a run-and-a-third before exiting with an apparent injury, Minnesota built a 7-0 lead by the fourth, and Nick Kurtz's three-run homer keyed a furious A's comeback that fell three runs short in an 11-8 loss to the Twins.
